column1: # W3C RDF 1.2 conformance allowlist: tests a provider is KNOWN not to pass, each with a justification.
# Columns (tab-separated): provider label (Jena | RDF4J) <TAB> W3C test IRI <TAB> reason <TAB> expected-failure regex
# Tests from manifests without @base are keyed from `test-data/...` (checkout-independent).
# Only listed tests may be skipped, and only when the observed failure signature (see
# Rdf12ConformanceRunner.failureSignature) contains a match of the row's regex. EVAL-MISMATCH marks an eval
# result that is not isomorphic to the expectation; ACCEPTED-INVALID-INPUT a negative test that parsed cleanly.
# An unlisted failure, a failure of a different kind, or a listed test that starts behaving correctly fails
# the build. Regenerate candidate rows with -PconformanceAllowlistProposal=<file>.
# EVAL-MISMATCH rows pin the fingerprint of the expected-vs-actual difference (blank nodes anonymised), so a
# different wrong result fails. JDK exceptions (e.g. NullPointerException) are pinned to their throwing frame.
# Language tags are compared exactly as written in the expected file (no case normalisation).
# Eval expectations are parsed by an independent reference parser (Jena RIOT, raw nodes) and compared as
# datasets, so provider parser bugs cannot cancel out.
# Blank-node graph names (TriG `_:g { }`): the Kastor RdfRepository API names graphs by IRI only, so both providers'
# parseDataset skolemizes them to `urn:kastor:skolem:` IRIs, which the harness compares as the blank-node graph
# RDF4J 5.3.2 (Rio) entries are upstream parser gaps, generated from a strict run and reviewed by category.
